<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:iteration}
If all edge weights are positive and at least one unsolved vertex is reachable, then any $f^*$ minimizing $D_t(f)$ over $\mathcal{F}_t$ satisfies
\[
  D_t(f^*)=\delta(s,f^*).
\]
Hence its shortest-path distance can be finalized.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
By the preceding inequalities, a path attaining $D_t(f^*)$ is globally shortest in $\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{U}_t)$. In particular, it is shortest among the paths to its own endpoint $f^*$, which form a subset of $\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{U}_t)$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
